nodes.name: Solvothermal synthesis of WO3-x
nodes.procedure: 0.5 g of WCl6 was first dissolved in 35 mL of anhydrous ethanol. The solution was transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave reactor after the WCl6 completely dissolved. Then, the mixture was heated at 180°C for 10 h. And the product was obtained by washing and filtering with deionized water and acetone. The WO3-x was obtained after freeze-drying.

nodes.name: CVD synthesis of WS2
nodes.procedure: Initially, 0.05g of tungsten trioxide with oxygen vacancies (WO3-x) and 0.75g of thiourea (CH4N2S) were loaded into the downstream and upstream boats of a tube furnace, respectively. Ar flow was introduced and stabilized for an hour. Subsequently, the mixture was annealed at 450°C for 2h to obtain WS2.

nodes.name: CVD partial sulfurization WS2/WO3-x-1
nodes.procedure: WO3-x (0.05g) and CH4N2S (0.3g) were placed in a tube furnace. The WO3-x was placed in the downstream magnetic boat and the CH4N2S was located upstream. Then, the Ar gas was introduced into the quartz tube to remove air for one hour, and the tube was held at 450°C for 2h. WO3-x sulfurized from 0.3g sulfur source was recorded as WS2/WO3-x-1.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ-2 show peaks corresponding to WS₂ (JCPDS 87-2417) and WO₃ (JCPDS 83-0950) crystal structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The structure of WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ-2 heterostructured catalyst was confirmed by X-ray diffraction spectroscopy (XRD) in Fig. 1a, where the peaks correspond to the crystal structures of WS₂ (JCPDS 87-2417) and WO₃ (JCPDS 83-0950).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM image of WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ-2 exhibits hexagonal nanosheet structure with rough and incomplete morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1b is the scanning electron microscope (SEM) image of the WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ heterostructure, exhibiting a hexagonal nanosheet structure with a rough and incomplete morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image of WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ-2 shows incomplete hexagonal nanosheet morphology consistent with SEM results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 1c, the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of the WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ-2 heterostructured catalyst still exhibits an incomplete hexagonal nanosheet morphology, which is in agreement with the SEM results.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals (002) crystal plane of WO₃ with lattice spacing 0.384 nm and (101) plane of WS₂ with 0.266 nm, with heterogeneous interfaces marked by red dotted lines and defect locations confirmed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 1d, the visible (002) crystal plane of WO₃ corresponds to a lattice spacing of 0.384 nm. Additionally, the (101) crystal plane of WS₂ has a lattice spacing of 0.266 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of W, O, and S elements in WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ-2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) element images in Fig. 1e, the uniform distribution of W, O, and S elements can be determined in the WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ-2 heterostructured catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR spectra show signals at g=2.003 assigned to oxygen vacancies, with stronger intensity for WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ-2 than WO₃₋ₓ indicating more oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 1f, WO₃₋ₓ and WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ-2 exhibit signals at g = 2.003, which are assigned to O vacancies. The signal intensity of the WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ-2 heterostructured catalyst is stronger than that of WO₃₋ₓ.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS W 4f spectrum of WS₂/WO₃₋ₓ-2 shows W⁴⁺ at 33.3 eV (4f₇/₂) and 35.4 eV (4f₅/₂), W⁵⁺ at 36.2 eV and 38.4 eV, W⁶⁺ at 36.7 eV and 38.9 eV with shifts indicating electron transfer from WO₃₋ₓ to WS₂; S 2p shows W-S bonds with positive shift; O 1s peaks at 531.2 eV (lattice oxygen), 531.8 eV (defect oxygen), 532.6 eV (chemisorbed oxygen) with larger defect oxygen peak area confirming more oxygen vacancies.
